passage:
A mountain school had weak internet for years. When heavy rain came, online classes often stopped.
One year, the school received a satellite internet system. Students could finally join video lessons, search information, and speak with guest teachers from other cities.
However, the principal reminded everyone that connection was only the beginning. Teachers still had to prepare good lessons. Students still had to ask questions and think.
The satellite brought the world closer, but it did not learn for them.
Technology can open a window. What students do after the window opens still depends on effort, curiosity, and guidance.
